newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas untraded, levels follow OTC sharply down.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas untraded, levels follow OTC sharply down.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures contract was untraded again on Thursday afternoon, but bids and offers ended well below the previous settlement level following a sharp fall on the physical market from lunchtime onwards, traders said.
Physical prices plunged in the early afternoon, traders said, with the year from October 1997 trading at 12.80 pence a therm after opening at 13.80 pence.
Although levels then bounced back slightly, prices were still heavily off during the period when the IPE was open.
A completely blank day on futures was avoided by a single trade done in the morning session. The contract has now seen only four trades, totalling 55 lots, done so far this week.

During the afternoon, bids and offers were frequently far apart. Around an hour into the session, there was at least a penny between bids and offers on every month except one, and the greatest gap was 2.20 pence a therm.

Bids and offers narrowed towards the close, but even so there was still a gap of 0.65 pence a therm between buyers and sellers on the front three months, all bid at 10.65 pence and offered at 11.30 pence a therm.
